WEARABLES CAN CAPTURE
  • Heart rate and beat-to-beat intervals
  • Movement and physical activity
  • Sleep; sometimes EDA, temperature, or GPS*
HRV CAN INDICATE
  • Autonomic regulation and recovery
  • Change relative to a person’s baseline
  • Not a direct reading of stress or emotion
HRV + EMA CAN CONNECT
  • When a response changed
  • What the participant reported
  • Which experience condition may matter

*Available indices depend on the device. Research-grade HRV requires validated beat-to-beat (RR/IBI) data and artifact cleaning.

FROM OUR JORDAN LAB WORK

From daily stress
to experience
measurement.

This multimodal approach has been applied to measure daily stress in naturalistic settings (Yao et al., 2024; Jordan et al., 2023; Greenwell et al., 2025).

In the experience industry, it can capture real-time physiological and self-reported indicators of stress, affective response, and satisfaction among both employees and guests.

Below, students learn to apply this method to compare, interpret, and redesign an experience.

FIELD TASK

Map arrival, waiting, participation, and exit. Select one touchpoint and define the experience response you expect to change.

ExamplesFestival entranceStadium gateTrail briefing
OPERATIONSQueue and crowd flowCompare single-line vs. guided entry.
GUEST EXPERIENCEWayfinding and service encountersCompare standard signs vs. journey prompts.
RISK + SAFETYBriefing and preparednessCompare verbal-only vs. practice-based briefing.
WORKFORCEStaff rotation and recoveryCompare continuous duty vs. scheduled recovery.
ONE METHOD, MANY SETTINGSEVENT×SPORT×ADVENTURE×OUTDOOR×TRAVEL
Measurement accuracy + classroom protocol +

Short comparison: two minutes seated stabilization, a five-minute resting baseline, and matched five-minute low-motion windows. Calculate RMSSD from cleaned RR intervals; pair every window with movement, a brief EMA, and field notes.

Interpret cautiously: breathing, posture, movement, temperature, caffeine, excitement, and individual differences influence HRV. A multi-day baseline is appropriate when the goal is a person’s usual HRV—not a within-session classroom comparison.
